allDirections.name: Triage Deck
allDirections.summary: A no-nonsense command surface for triaging a flood of tickets — razor-thin lines, chunky status flags, and every millisecond accounted for.
allDirections.typographyVoice: Display: Space Grotesk (geometric, technical, slightly squared) for headings and ticket IDs. Body: DM Sans (neutral, compact, legible) for descriptions and metadata.
signatureMoves: Triage pegs: each ticket row has a left-edge triangular notch filled with the priority color (accent, amber, slate) — a physical flag you scan instantly.
Response timer in oversized tabular numerals with a hairline rule under the minutes; pulses once when the threshold passes.
Assignee avatars as hard-edged squares with a 2px status border; hover reveals a keyboard shortcut hint (e.g. [A] to assign).
Multiselect mode slides in a 'stack' counter — a pinned card that aggregates selected rows and shows a total at the bottom edge.
Hairline dividers between rows are replaced by 4px gaps; only group sections get a 1px top border, keeping the scan path clean.

allDirections.name: Soft Landing
allDirections.summary: A friendly, approachable triage experience that wraps busy work in soft shapes and gentle motion — like a support team's favourite notepad, but smarter.
allDirections.typographyVoice: Display: Bricolage Grotesque (characterful, rounded, modern) for headings and empty states. Body: Instrument Sans (warm, readable, slightly humanist) for ticket content.
signatureMoves: Presence rings: avatars are full pills with a 3px accent ring that gently expands when the agent is actively typing; no other notification sound.
Priority labels as hand-rolled chips: solid accent for urgent, 40% tinted surface for normal, and a pale neutral for low — all with pill shapes.
Stacked timeline cards for each conversation: each reply is a soft-edged layer that lifts and casts a tiny shadow when hovered; the sending animation is a springy drop from above.
Overdue timers become a soft, breathing dot beside the ticket that expands and contracts at 1.5s — a heartbeat, not a siren.
Empty state is a custom sketch-style mailbox with a curved lid and a small sprout; the CTA is a pill button that wiggles on first hover.

allDirections.name: Calm Clock
allDirections.summary: A composed, stately workspace for teams that value precision and calm — every ticket feels like part of a well-orchestrated day, with time as the conductor.
allDirections.typographyVoice: Display: Sora (clean, geometric, slightly rounded) for headings and timer displays. Body: General Sans (neutral, professional, refined) for long-form ticket text.
signatureMoves: Tonal sections: the inbox is divided by soft washes of the accent at 6%–12% tint for priority groups, creating background rhythm without hard lines.
Rotating timer: each ticket's response timer appears as a thin ring around its avatar, with a small arc draining clockwise; the arc turns accent when the deadline is near.
Stately slide-in: new tickets enter from the right side with a 300ms ease, and their priority label fades in after a 80ms delay, creating a patient reveal.
Connection dots: conversation rows are linked by a thin vertical line with a dot per participant; the line draws itself as the conversation updates.
Focus modal: clicking a ticket opens a centered panel with the timer as an oversized numeral at the top, plus the full thread below; the background dims to a deeper tonal shade.
